column2: req_desc

Room-first floor plan
The plan page draws the nine rooms in plan order as outlined shapes, each named for its room and the scene that owns it at the scrubbed time, with a scene legend beneath.

Time-of-day scrubber
A single time-of-day slider under the plan moves across the chosen household day with the published key steps, pointer and touch dragging, and day controls, as detailed in Interactions.

Shareable plan address
The address bar always carries the scrubbed day and time with its offset, and opening that address or reloading shows the same view.

Plan sweep
Crossing a scheduled change fills the affected rooms one by one in plan order with the published stagger and duration, and each legend count steps by one as each fill lands.

Reduced-motion plan
With reduced motion on, fills, room names and legend counts switch in one frame, and the 'At this time' list and the 'Plan time' announcement carry the same room-to-scene facts in both modes.

Newest scrub wins
A step taken while an earlier sweep is still running cancels its remaining fills, and the plan, legend and list all end on the newest time.

Published plan layouts
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 the plan page shows its published order and columns with no horizontal overflow, and closed drawers and sheets are hidden and cannot take focus.

Day plan API
GET /api/plan returns the household day's length, start owners and every change with its local time and offset, using the schedule version in force that day and any guest scenes.

Plan sweep look
The floor plan reads as a lamplit blueprint: cyan hairline rooms with dimension ticks on near-black navy, warm fills only for scene-held rooms, and a scrubber with hour ticks and the now marker.

Plan sweep journey
The household owner opens the plan, scrubs from morning to bedtime, copies the address into a new tab and sees the same rooms and scenes.

Household status and socket
GET /api/status and the /api/socket stream publish the hub's time, each room's live scene and service health, pushed within one second of any change and at least every 15 seconds.

Server-placed now
The 'now' marker, hub time, the scrubber's opening position and every room's live scene come only from the server's status, whatever the device clock or zone says.

Simulation API
The simulation endpoints set the hub clock and let simulated devices report state and go offline, with every effect visible in the API and the socket.

Named live regions
Device and scene changes from the socket update the screen in place without a reload and are announced in the 'Device updates' and 'Scene changes' regions with the published copy.

Room inspector
Choosing a room shows its live scene, its devices with their state and the day's plan for that room, as a side column at 1280x800 and as a sheet at smaller sizes.

Device state API
PUT /api/devices/{id}/state changes a light, plug or thermostat with the published fields and limits, bumps its revision and broadcasts the new state.

Device sheet
Each device has a details sheet with the controls for its kind, reachable by keyboard, which shows the server's latest state.

Refused toggle rolls back
An optimistic switch change the server refuses returns to the server's state and shows the device-offline copy.

Newest device action wins
Toggling again while a request is pending or the device sheet is closing ends with both screen and server on the last choice.

Scenes drive devices
Whenever a room's live scene changes, the server sets that room's online lights and thermostats to the scene's settings and leaves plugs and cameras as they are.

Live house journey
The household owner opens the plan on a tablet whose clock runs 47 minutes fast, turns the kitchen lights off and on from the inspector and sees each change land in place.

Fall-back day timeline
On the household's fall-back day the plan and scrubber span 25 hours with the 01:00 hour drawn twice and labelled by its offset, and spring-forward days span 23 hours.

Repeated hour runs once
A slot inside the repeated hour runs once, at its first occurrence, and owns its rooms through the second pass of that hour.

Skipped hour runs at 03:00
On the spring-forward day a slot inside the skipped hour runs at 03:00 and the plan shows it there.

Run ledger
The server records each slot occurrence once when the running hub clock reaches it, never for occurrences skipped by a clock move, and lists them by household day in GET /api/runs.

Fall-back night journey
The household owner scrubs Sunday 1 November 2026 through both 01:30s and later reads that day's runs, showing 'Night low' ran once.

Household day boundaries
Runs, clips and notices group by the household's local day in America/Chicago, and 'today' is the hub's local day, whatever zone the browser uses.

Day log page
The Day log page lists a chosen household day's runs and clips, defaulting to the hub's today and updating clip rows in place.

Day log journey
The household owner, browsing from a laptop set to another zone late in the evening, opens the Day log and sees only the runs and clips that belong to the household's today.

Effective-dated schedule versions
Each schedule save carries a from date and creates or replaces the version for that date, and every day uses the latest version whose from date is on or before it.

From date rules
A from date must be the hub's today or later and at most 366 days after it, with the published field errors otherwise.

Schedule editor sheet
The schedule editor sheet edits slot times, scenes and rooms plus the from date, and saves with the published pending and success copy.

Effective edit journey
The second adult moves weekday 'Wake' from 06:40 to 06:10 from Monday 9 November 2026, and scrubbing Friday 6 November still shows 06:40 while that Monday shows 06:10.

One winning schedule save
Saves to one schedule carry the revision the editor read, and of any concurrent saves with the same revision exactly one succeeds and the rest get the 409 schedule_changed answer.

Losing editor sees the winner
The losing editor shows the conflict copy with a Reload schedule button that loads the winner's slots, and open plans repaint to the winner's slots.

Scene catalogue API
GET, POST and PUT on /api/scenes list, create and change scenes with a unique name, one of six tints, a brightness and an optional setpoint.

Scene sheet
The New scene and Edit scene sheets create and change scenes with field errors shown beside their fields and the published pending and success copy.

Keyboard scene journey
Using only the keyboard, the household owner creates a scene, adds it to rooms in a weekend slot, scrubs to that slot and opens a clip sheet, with focus trapped and returned at each sheet.

Guest scene states
Guest scenes move scheduled → active → ended or cancelled under the published transition rules, with 409 answers for overlaps and for cancelling a closed guest scene.

Guest scene ends on the server
The server ends a guest scene at its end instant, inclusive, with no browser open, returns the room to its scheduled scene and pushes the change on the socket.

Guest request replay
A guest scene request repeated with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer, and the same key with a different body gets 409 idempotency_conflict.

Guest scene journey
The household owner gives the spare room the 'Guest welcome' scene until 11:00 and watches it hand back to the schedule at 11:00:00 hub time.

Camera clip intake
A simulated camera announces a clip with its declared byte size and then submits the bytes, which the server stores byte for byte under the published object key.

Storage-confirmed clips
A clip becomes stored and playable only after object storage reports the object at the declared size, and a size mismatch is rejected for good.

Clip sheet and Play
Clip rows show the storing copy until the clip is stored, and the clip sheet's Play button is enabled only for stored clips, updating in place.

Clip storage outage
While object storage is unreachable, clip bytes get 503, clips stay storing, nothing is marked stored and every page shows the storage banner.

Clip review journey
The household owner sees a new porch camera clip appear as storing, waits for it to become playable and plays it from the clip sheet.

Notice outbox
Every household notice is written to the outbox first and sent by email exactly once, within ten seconds while mail is up, as qualified in Services.

Household notice messages
The server sends plain-text notices with no links when it ends a guest scene, when an effective-dated edit takes effect and when a clip is stored, with the published subjects and bodies.

Mail outage
While mail is unreachable, notices stay queued, nothing is sent, the Notices page shows the mail banner, and each queued notice is sent exactly once when mail is back.

Notices page
The Notices page lists every notice newest first with its subject, recipient and queued or sent state, updating in place.

Run manifest and health
/app/run.json installs, builds and serves the app on the published port, and the health path answers 200 with {"status":"ok"} once ready.

Configuration from environment
Every service address and credential is read from the published environment variables at start and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Same-origin server boundary
The server enforces the published body limits and content types, refuses cross-origin writes and socket connections, and never serves source, manifest or environment files.

One error shape
Every API error uses the one published JSON error shape and the single published precedence order.

Keyboard-complete sheets
Every sheet and drawer opens and works from the keyboard, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside while open, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Readable, tappable controls
Every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels and all text and control edges meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on the dark ground.

No decorative loops
Nothing on any page moves while the user is idle except changes the server pushes, and sheets open and close within the published time.

Nocturnal blueprint look
Every page sits on a near-black navy blueprint sheet with a faint grid, cyan hairlines, pale ink, warm lamp fills only for scenes and coral only for alerts, in the published typefaces with tabular mono numerals.

Honest service wiring
Clip state, notice state and schedule revisions come from real PostgreSQL, MinIO and SMTP calls, with no in-memory stand-ins or self-reported success.
/app/run.json exists with exactly the string keys install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package with its version and licence, plus every bundled font and icon set. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree as npm ls --omit=dev --all --json reports it.
Shipped packages and bundled assets use only these licences: MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
PostgreSQL and MinIO are the only datastores. No SQLite, Redis, embedded database or files used as a database.
The provided development service configuration and its credentials stay unchanged.
/app/package-lock.json is committed and the install command uses npm ci.
Pages load no resources from other origins. Fonts and icons are served by the app itself.
